newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Stg to struggle at 2.9825/50 congestion.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Stg to struggle at 2.9825/50 congestion.

text.p: Sterling's attempts to eclipse its recent six-year high will run into strong resistance at 2.9825/50 marks, technical analysts said.
In European morning trading, the pound will stick to a consolidation range between the high at 2.9760 marks and support around 2.9640/50.
The pound will struggle to leave that range ahead of the Bank of England's decision on interest rates, to be announced at 1100 GMT.
"The pound is looking extremely overbought at these levels, so any progress on the upside will be quite difficult," said Mark Ostwald, technical analyst at Monument Derivatives.
A break above the 2.9760 high would be needed to assert pressure on the upside. But Ostwald pointed to a strong barrier in the 2.9825/50 band, a congestion zone dating back to late 1991.
"Even if it breaks the high it will run into trouble there," said Ostwald.
At 0710 GMT sterling/mark was at 2.9743/53 and $1.6839/46 compared with 2.9671/81 and $1.6833/39 in late Europe Wednesday.
Traders said sterling was likely to pop higher on any rate announcement but profit-taking was likely to emerge soon.
The immediate key support on the downside will be 2.9480, the low from Tuesday, ahead of Monday's trough at 2.9320.
Some chartists see a need for a larger correction in sterling/mark to 2.85 before it resumes its rally for a stab at the psychological barrier at 3.00.
Eddie Matts, director at Capital Management, said there was near-term support at 2.9640 ahead of 2.9480 and 2.9300. He advised to rebuy on a drop to 2.9300/50 with stops at 2.91.
Cable was locked into a range between support at $1.6820 and resistance at $1.6900, which capped the pound on Wednesday and left Tuesday's near seven-month high at $1.6959 out of sight.
